paper_summary: Japanese-language paper (J. Soc. Mat. Sci. Japan, 53(9), 950-955, 2004) by Todo, Komeda and Arakawa on the effect of CTBN liquid-rubber modification on the fracture properties of glass-microballoon-filled epoxy (GM/EP) used as an aerospace encapsulant. Four materials were cast (neat Epikote 828, rubber-modified 828R, GM-filled 828G and GM-filled rubber-modified 828RG) with 10 wt% surface-treated 3M A16 glass microballoons, cured 16 h at 120 C, and tested in three-point bending and SENB fracture toughness at quasi-static and impact (1 m/s) loading rates. Rubber modification lowered the flexural modulus and strength of the GM-filled epoxy but raised its absorbed fracture energy by 90% (quasi-static) and 46% (impact) and increased GIC by roughly 2-3x; SEM showed GM/matrix interfacial debonding plus shear-band formation around the 1-2 um rubber particles as the toughening mechanisms.
extraction_notes: IMPORTANT - very little quantitative data is recoverable from this text file. Table I (weight mixing ratio) and Table II (relative density and bending mechanical properties E, S, U) and Fig. 5 (KIC and GIC results) are bitmap images; only their captions survive in the extracted text, so no absolute values of flexural modulus, bending strength, absorbed energy, relative density or fracture toughness are readable. Per the extraction rules those fields are left null rather than estimated from figures. The only quantitative statements in the running text are RELATIVE changes caused by CTBN modification of the GM-filled resin: flexural modulus down 10-30% (larger drop for the GM-filled grades), quasi-static bending strength down 16%, impact bending strength down 4%, quasi-static absorbed fracture energy up 90%, impact absorbed fracture energy up 46%, quasi-static GIC up ~2x and impact GIC up ~3x; 10 wt% GM roughly halves the density relative to neat 828. These are recorded in microstructure_notes / specimen_notes and quoted as evidence but cannot be turned into absolute property values. Fracture toughness (KIC, GIC) has no field in this schema, so the SENB fracture-toughness test conditions are not given separate records; they are described here instead (SENB, quasi-static 1 mm/min on a servo-hydraulic machine and impact 1 m/s on an instrumented drop-weight tower, per ASTM D5045-91a). Records are given only for the two GM-filled (syntactic) materials, 828G and 828RG, at the two three-point-bending loading rates; the unfilled controls 828 and 828R contain no hollow particles and are not recorded. Mean particle size is stated as a 30-70 um range rather than a single value, so particle_mean_diameter_um is left null (full size distribution 15-135 um, wall thickness 1 um, particle true density 0.16 g/cm3, particle crush strength 3.5 MPa). Crosshead/impact speeds are recorded in specimen_notes because specimen dimensions (Fig. 1) are also an image, so strain rate in 1/s cannot be computed. Test temperature is not stated anywhere and is left null.

records.sample_label: 828G (Epikote 828 + 10 wt% GM, no rubber) - quasi-static bending

processing.matrix_name: Epikote 828 bisphenol-A epoxy (Yuka Shell) with modified-amine hardener B-002
processing.particle_grade: 3M (Sumitomo 3M) A16 surface-treated glass microballoons; size distribution 15-135 um, mean 30-70 um, wall thickness 1 um, true density 0.16 g/cm3, crush strength 3.5 MPa

structure.microstructure_notes: Filling with 10 wt% GM lowers the density to about half that of neat 828 (i.e. relative density ~0.5); the absolute value is only given in Table II, which is an image. SEM of the quasi-static fracture surface shows good GM/matrix interfacial adhesion, with the crack propagating mainly along the GM/resin interface, linking adjacent microballoons.

test.specimen_notes: Three-point bending of a beam specimen (100 mm long) at a quasi-static crosshead speed of 10 mm/min on a servo-hydraulic machine; specimen cross-section given only in Fig. 1 (image), so strain rate in 1/s cannot be computed. E, S and U were measured but their values appear only in Table II, which is an image.

records.sample_label: 828G (Epikote 828 + 10 wt% GM, no rubber) - impact bending, 1 m/s

processing.matrix_name: Epikote 828 bisphenol-A epoxy (Yuka Shell) with modified-amine hardener B-002
processing.particle_grade: 3M (Sumitomo 3M) A16 surface-treated glass microballoons; size distribution 15-135 um, mean 30-70 um, wall thickness 1 um, true density 0.16 g/cm3, crush strength 3.5 MPa

structure.microstructure_notes: Same material as the quasi-static 828G record; 10 wt% GM roughly halves the density relative to neat 828. Under impact the crack runs straighter and more bare epoxy fracture surface is exposed than under quasi-static loading.

また,衝撃弾性率は準静的弾性率より高い値となっている.

records.sample_label: 828RG (CTBN rubber-modified Epikote 828 + 10 wt% GM) - quasi-static bending

processing.matrix_name: CTBN-modified Epikote 828 bisphenol-A epoxy (Yuka Shell) with modified-amine hardener B-002
processing.particle_grade: 3M (Sumitomo 3M) A16 surface-treated glass microballoons; size distribution 15-135 um, mean 30-70 um, wall thickness 1 um, true density 0.16 g/cm3, crush strength 3.5 MPa
processing.additional_fillers: CTBN 1300x9 carboxyl-terminated liquid NBR rubber (Ube Kosan), precipitating 1-2 um rubber particles in the epoxy matrix; blend ratio given only in Table I (image)

structure.microstructure_notes: 10 wt% GM roughly halves the density relative to neat 828. 1-2 um CTBN rubber particles are dispersed in the matrix; the quasi-static fracture surface shows pronounced GM/matrix interfacial debonding and ~100 nm wide shear bands linking the rubber particles.

test.specimen_notes: Three-point bending at a quasi-static crosshead speed of 10 mm/min. Relative to 828G, rubber modification lowered the quasi-static bending strength by 16% and the flexural modulus by 10-30%, while raising the quasi-static absorbed fracture energy by 90%. Absolute values appear only in Table II (image).

records.sample_label: 828RG (CTBN rubber-modified Epikote 828 + 10 wt% GM) - impact bending, 1 m/s

processing.matrix_name: CTBN-modified Epikote 828 bisphenol-A epoxy (Yuka Shell) with modified-amine hardener B-002
processing.particle_grade: 3M (Sumitomo 3M) A16 surface-treated glass microballoons; size distribution 15-135 um, mean 30-70 um, wall thickness 1 um, true density 0.16 g/cm3, crush strength 3.5 MPa
processing.additional_fillers: CTBN 1300x9 carboxyl-terminated liquid NBR rubber (Ube Kosan), precipitating 1-2 um rubber particles in the epoxy matrix

structure.microstructure_notes: 10 wt% GM roughly halves the density relative to neat 828. Unlike the quasi-static case, no GM/matrix interfacial debonding is seen on the impact fracture surface; shear bands around the rubber particles are still present and are the dominant toughening mechanism.

test.specimen_notes: Three-point bending impact fracture test at 1 m/s on an instrumented drop-weight system. Relative to 828G, rubber modification lowered the impact bending strength by only 4% while raising the impact absorbed fracture energy by 46%. In the companion SENB tests 828RG was the only material whose KIC and GIC increased with loading rate. Absolute values appear only in Table II and Fig. 5 (images).

evidence.quote: GM充填材にゴム変性を施すと,曲げ弾性率と曲げ強度は低下するが,準静的吸収破壊エネルギーは90%,衝撃吸収破壊エネルギーは46%上昇する.
GM充填材にゴム変性を施すと,破壊じん性は大きく向上し,特に臨界ひずみエネルギー解放率は2～3倍に上昇する.
